scoring.priority: critical when RPN >= 300; high when RPN >= 180 or severity >= 9; medium when RPN >= 80; low otherwise

risks.failure_mode: An external side effect is applied more than once after an ambiguous crash because a consumer or provider does not honor the idempotency/reconciliation contract.
risks.effect: Duplicate payment, publication, hardware command or other irreversible business action despite a correct at-least-once runtime.
causes: Consumer handler treats task completion as exactly-once delivery.
Provider has no idempotency key or reconciliation endpoint.
Crash occurs after the provider accepts the effect but before Axiom durably commits the result.
current_controls: Persist intent/task before external execution.
Stable durable effect/task identity.
Explicit at-least-once contract and ambiguous-side-effect classification.
Flow crash/reopen equivalence and no-resurrection tests.
risks.mitigation: Make the production reference application prove provider idempotency plus reconciliation across the accepted-effect/before-result-commit crash window; document the integration contract as a release-gated example.
exit_evidence: Reference application injects the ambiguous crash window and converges without duplicate business application.
Expected history explicitly distinguishes delivery attempts from business application.
Production documentation states the non-exactly-once boundary at the effect adapter.
risks.review_trigger: Any new external-effect API, compensation primitive or production profile change.

risks.failure_mode: A multi-host custom Store violates CAS, inbox deduplication, leasing/fencing, ordering or transaction boundaries under concurrent coordinators.
risks.effect: Lost events, duplicate execution, stale-worker commits, split-brain scheduling or corrupted durable history.
causes: The Store interface is implementable over systems with different isolation guarantees.
There is no first-party networked transactional backend demonstrating the complete multi-host contract.
A backend may pass happy-path tests while violating contention or crash semantics.
current_controls: Store conformance suites and durable state-machine tests.
Explicit worker/attempt/lease fencing.
Fail-closed plan/schema identity.
Pebble/File backends characterize single-owner/shared-filesystem behavior rather than claiming generic distributed semantics.
risks.mitigation: Implement the first-party PostgreSQL Store and qualify it with multi-connection contention, rollback, stale-worker fencing, crash/reconnect, isolation and migration/upgrade fault injection; extend the integration gate to require backend capability evidence.
exit_evidence: PostgreSQL backend passes Store conformance and adversarial multi-connection suites.
Isolation level and transaction boundaries are documented and executable.
Stale workers cannot commit after lease loss across independent processes.
risks.review_trigger: Any Store SPI change, new durable backend, leasing change or multi-host topology change.

risks.failure_mode: Behaviorally different orchestration surfaces drift while sharing similar names or low-level concepts, causing an integration to assume equivalence that does not exist.
risks.effect: Retry timing, lease expiry, persistence, replay or recovery semantics differ across supported paths and produce inconsistent behavior under failure.
causes: Core, Flow and ADGO intentionally remain separate runtimes.
Some durable concepts are structurally similar but have different state-machine ownership or clock domains.
Documentation or future refactoring can accidentally erase intentional semantic differences.
current_controls: Executable characterization before sharing primitives.
AST architecture anti-drift tests.
Only durabletime.NowSource is currently shared as a proven behavior-identical leaf.
Retry/backoff and lease/fencing remain engine-owned after explicit non-equivalence proof.
risks.mitigation: Make the Algorithm Integration Matrix encode runtime ownership and semantic differences, then gate new production features on an explicit surface/API/persistence/failure-semantics declaration.
exit_evidence: Integration matrix distinguishes Core, Flow and ADGO ownership for each durable primitive.
CI fails when a production feature loses its runtime/API/test linkage.
Anti-drift tests remain green after any shared-primitive extraction.
risks.review_trigger: Any extraction into internal shared packages or any claim that two runtimes provide equivalent semantics.

risks.failure_mode: A consumer chooses a technically valid but semantically wrong combination of App/Runtime/Flow/Engine/Host/Store/Policy/Scheduler components and unintentionally bypasses durability or hard controls.
risks.effect: Production deployment runs with weaker durability, risk, admission, budget or recovery guarantees than the operator believes.
causes: Large number of individually valid entry points.
Advanced capabilities are optional and composition-dependent.
The public surface does not yet funnel common deployments through a small set of supported profiles.
current_controls: OpenProduction assembly exists for ADGO.
Architecture documentation separates embedded and production boundaries.
Hard admission checks precede scheduler utility inside ADGO.
risks.mitigation: Publish Embedded, Durable Single Node and Distributed Production profiles with one canonical composition path each; prove them through conformance tests and a full production reference application; tier the stable API.
exit_evidence: Each supported profile has one canonical constructor/configuration path and explicit guarantees/non-guarantees.
Reference application exercises advanced controls together, including crash/reopen behavior.
Stable facade is mechanically classified separately from advanced/SPI APIs.
risks.review_trigger: Any new top-level constructor, production capability or public orchestration entry point.

risks.failure_mode: One logical coordinator decision observes multiple clock domains or multiple time snapshots, crossing a due/expiry boundary inside a single decision.
risks.effect: False deadlock, early/late retry, premature lease expiry, duplicate work or stale result acceptance near timing boundaries.
causes: Runtime contains semantic clocks, operational wall clocks, timers and durable deadlines with deliberately different ownership.
A helper can accidentally call real time instead of the governing clock.
Readiness and terminal classification can become TOCTOU-sensitive if time is sampled more than once.
current_controls: Explicit durabletime clock inventory and anti-drift checks.
One semantic-time snapshot per logically coupled ADGO Advance decision.
Deterministic deadline-crossing regression for F-026.
Lease/retry characterization tests preserve intentional Core/ADGO differences.
risks.mitigation: Represent clock-domain ownership in the integration matrix and require new time-dependent production features to declare their governing clock, persistence boundary and deterministic boundary tests before DONE.
exit_evidence: Every time-dependent production feature is linked to an explicit clock domain in the integration matrix.
Boundary tests cover equality at due/lease expiry and clock advancement within scheduling decisions.
CI prevents direct semantic-time bypasses in shared durable primitives.
risks.review_trigger: Any timer, retry, lease, schedule, timeout or clock abstraction change.

risks.failure_mode: A software or plan upgrade creates durable state that cannot be safely interpreted, migrated or rolled back across versions.
risks.effect: Fail-closed production outage, stranded executions, incorrect live repinning or irreversible history/state incompatibility.
causes: Many serialized surfaces evolve independently.
Plan/schema identity is strict, so unsafe compatibility is rejected rather than guessed.
A backend migration can be correct in isolation but incompatible with live task/inbox/version state.
current_controls: Explicit plan ID/version/digest pinning.
Fail-closed persisted format markers and compatibility fixtures.
Quiescent-point validation for ADGO plan migration.
Serialized-surfaces inventory and versioning policy.
risks.mitigation: Make migration/upgrade compatibility a required PostgreSQL conformance scenario and an integration-completeness declaration for every feature that changes durable state.
exit_evidence: Cross-version fixtures cover supported durable surfaces and fail closed on unsupported future schemas.
Networked backend upgrade tests include live historical versions, inbox and task state.
Every new production feature declares durable-state and migration impact before DONE.
risks.review_trigger: Any serialized schema, plan migration rule, durable backend format or release compatibility change.

risks.failure_mode: A broad stable-looking exported surface freezes low-level implementation contracts or is accidentally broken while higher-level guarantees remain unchanged.
risks.effect: Consumer breakage, inability to evolve internals safely, duplicated integration patterns and increased release risk.
causes: Large pre-v1 exported symbol set.
Advanced extension points and common-path APIs are not yet clearly tiered.
Consumers can depend directly on low-level infrastructure primitives.
current_controls: Golden public API manifest gate.
Deprecation inventory and pre-v1 compatibility policy.
Typed error taxonomy and API guide.
risks.mitigation: Classify exports into stable facade, advanced, extension SPI, deprecated and internalization candidates while preserving mechanical compatibility checks.
exit_evidence: All exported symbols have an API tier.
Common integrations can avoid low-level SPI types.
Compatibility gate remains cross-platform deterministic.
risks.review_trigger: Any exported symbol addition/removal or compatibility-policy change.

risks.failure_mode: The mechanical API compatibility gate produces platform-dependent symbol manifests and blocks or misclassifies a release.
risks.effect: False release blocker, reduced trust in the compatibility gate or pressure to weaken a safety-critical CI check.
causes: Platform-specific representation such as line endings, path separators, ordering or tooling output.
Golden manifest comparison is intentionally strict.
current_controls: Public API manifest is mechanically generated and compared.
Operating protocol forbids weakening a red gate merely to regain green.
Recent main commits target Windows traversal and line-ending normalization, but the authoritative plan still requires full cross-platform qualification.
risks.mitigation: Complete deterministic cross-platform characterization and qualify the exact fixed SHA on Windows, Linux and macOS without suppressing real API changes.
exit_evidence: Same source revision yields the same symbol set on Windows, Linux and macOS.
A fixture proves representation normalization does not hide removed or modified symbols.
Exact fixed SHA passes the full matrix and race gates.
risks.review_trigger: Any API manifest extractor, Go version, line-ending or path-normalization change.

risks.failure_mode: Unprotected main permits an unqualified or non-reviewed change to bypass the repository's intended release and architecture gates.
risks.effect: Authoritative main can temporarily contain behavior that has not satisfied the required CI/security/quality/module gates.
causes: Branch protection is disabled outside the repository content.
Process discipline is currently the main enforcement boundary.
current_controls: Living MASTER_PLAN qualification protocol.
CI, security, quality-loop and module-checksum workflows.
No-force-push rule and exact-SHA qualification discipline.
risks.mitigation: Enable branch protection/rulesets requiring the repository's qualification gates and prohibit direct unqualified updates to main.
exit_evidence: GitHub branch/ruleset configuration requires the intended checks before main changes.
Direct unqualified push path is mechanically blocked.
risks.review_trigger: Any branch protection, required-check or release-governance change.
